COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
1 CLCON No. 218 of 2024
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. B.P. Nautiyal, Senior Advocate 
through video conferencing assisted by Mr. 
Mohd. Matlub, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. Rahul Verma, Additional 
Advocate General for the State.
The petitioners have brought to the 
notice of the Court the willful disobedience 
of the Court’s order dated 14.09.2015, 
passed in Writ Petition (M/S) No. 1192 of 
2015 and judgment dated 18.03.2024, 
passed in Special Appeal No. 574 of 2015, 
State of Uttarakhand and others Vs. M/s 
Nutech Vainish Udyog, Minikireti and 
others.
The response affidavit has already 
been filed.
The Court had required the 
respondent no.1 to join the proceedings 
through video conferencing because on the 
earlier occasion the Court was told that the 
modification application has been filed by 
the respondents. Filing of the modification 
application may not stall the proceedings 
of contempt.
Today, respondent no.1 has joined 
the proceedings through video 
conferencing. He submits that Special 
Leave Petition (Diary No.69950 of 2025) 
has been filed in the Hon’ble Supreme 
Court. He also submits that the 
respondents would honor the order of the 
Court. If the petitioners or any of them 
have deposited any excess stamp duty, 
they could produce the document to that 
effect and the money may be returned. He 
submits that, in fact, the petitioners have 
not deposited any excess amount. This fact is disputed by learned 
counsel for the petitioners.
Be it as it may, since it is stated that 
Special Leave Petition is preferred in the 
Hon’ble Supreme Court. The matter is 
deferred.
List on 26.02.2026.
The respondent no.1 need not appear 
personally, until further required by this 
Court.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 04.12.2025
Jitendra

MS NU Tech Varnish Udyog
--Petitioner
 Versus
R K Sudhanshu and another
--Respondents
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. B.P.Nautiyal, learned Senior 
Advocate assisted by Mr. Mohd. Matloob, 
learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. Rahul Verma, learned Addl. A.G.
for the State.
3. The subject matter of the present 
contempt petition is the order passed by 
Writ Court dated 14.09.2015 passed in 
WPMS No. 1192 of 2015, which was 
affirmed by the Division Bench of this Court 
and also by the Hon’ble Apex Court. 
4. From perusal of the record, it 
transpires that the Modification Application 
has been moved, after dismissal of the SLP,
before the Division Bench of this Court, that 
too was dismissed by the Division Bench of 
this Court. The Special Leave Petition was 
filed against the order, by which the 
Modification Application was rejected. The 
said SLP was dismissed by the Hon’ble Apex 
Court on 07.09.2026. 5. After dismissal of the SLP against the 
order passed by the Division Bench of this 
Court in the Modification Application, this 
Court vide order dated 09.09.2026 expected
the contemnors to comply with the order 
without any further delay within two weeks.
6. But today, instead of compliance of the 
order, learned counsel appearing 
for the respondents/contemnors seeks 
adjournment on the ground that the review 
against the order dated 07.09.2026 before 
Apex Court has been filed on 25.09.2026 
which was given the Diary No.59745 of 
2026. 
7. From looking at the history of the case,
it appears that the respondents/contemnors
are adamant not to comply with the order 
passed by the Writ Court. By hook and 
crook they want the matter to linger on. The 
review petition against the dismissal of the 
modification is no remedy in the eyes of law. 
This Court is of the view that this is attempt 
to violate and circumvent the order passed 
by Writ Court. It is also denial of justice to 
petitioner. 
8. In such view of the matter, the 
respondent/contemnor No.1 shall remain 
present physically before this Court on 
06.10.2026 or comply with the order by 
06.10.2026.
9. Put up on 06.10.2026.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 28.09.2026
Nahid

3. Pursuant to order dated 28.09.2026 passed by this

Secretary, Forest Department is present before this Court

4. The reason for his personal attendance was non￾compliance of the order passed by Writ Court in the year

5. Mr. R.K. Sudhanshu gives assurance to this Court 
that they are sincere about compliance of the order and 
the same would be complied with within hundred days as

6. This Court is vigilant of the fact that this matter is of
